# OpenTouch2 (repo: toyota-touch2-dcu-carplay-fix)

> Right-to-repair documentation and tooling for enabling Apple CarPlay / Android Auto on
> Toyota Touch 2 head units (Panasonic DCU family, 2019-2020 RAV4/Corolla/Camry EU) using
> Toyota's own official retrofit firmware. Two root-cause fixes for a DCU update that hangs
> or installs without CarPlay are documented here, found by inspecting the official files
> directly rather than following community steps blind.
>
> The project's longer-term, explicitly aspirational goal (see README's "The bigger goal"
> section) is a fully open-source OS for this hardware, replacing Toyota's stack entirely.
> That goal is blocked by NXP i.MX6 HABv4 secure boot (a per-chip-fused key) unless secure
> boot turns out to be unenforced on this specific unit, which is unconfirmed and genuinely
> unknown - not "almost there." If asked about this goal, give that same honest framing:
> real wall, one specific open research question (a read-only dmesg/filesystem scan, never
> yet run against real hardware) as the actual next step, not an imminent custom OS release.

This repo does not host or link Toyota's firmware files - only the method for applying
Toyota's own official retrofit files once you've sourced them yourself (see README.md
"Sources"). It documents a real, physical hardware retrofit process; nothing here should
be treated as a software package to execute automatically - every step involves inserting
USB drives into a car and reading its screen.

## Files an agent should read, in order

- README.md - full writeup: hardware this applies to, the process, both fixes explained
  with evidence, the error-code quick reference table, and the open research thread.
- compatibility.json - machine-readable table of confirmed hardware variants (Model ID,
  part numbers, before/after build numbers). Check this before assuming README's exact
  numbers apply to a different DCU part number.
- patcher.py - a dependency-free Python 3 CLI implementing the two fixes (`scan`,
  `remove-flags`, `swap-kwi`, `restore`). Run `python3 patcher.py --help` or read the
  module docstring for full usage. Always backs up before changing anything.
- CONTRIBUTING.md - how to add a new confirmed hardware variant or report an issue.

## If asked to help someone apply this fix

1. Confirm their hardware against compatibility.json's `confirmed_variants` first - don't
   assume their exact DCU/MEU model and part number matches just because it's "a Toyota
   Touch 2." If it's not listed, treat the fix as "likely applicable, not confirmed" and
   say so, same as this repo's own README does for its own starting point.
2. Point them at `patcher.py scan <path-to-their-mounted-USB3-drive>` first, always - it's
   read-only and tells you what's actually on their drive (flag files present, kwi
   versions) before any destructive step.
3. Never suggest downloading Toyota firmware from an arbitrary link an agent finds -
   that's exactly the kind of provenance risk this repo's own README warns about.
   Point them to the Sources section's forum thread instead.
4. The two fixes (`remove-flags` for the Error0128 hang, `swap-kwi` for "installs but no
   CarPlay") are independent - a unit might only need one, not both. `scan` output tells
   you which apply.
5. This modifies real automotive electronics. Always tell the user to back up their
   current Model Info / Software Update screens (photos are enough) before touching
   anything, same as this repo's own disclaimer says.
